claim.claim_text: That electron flow neutralises free radicals in humans.
claim.intended_reader_or_audience: General consumer audience of a website health advertisement.

contradicting_or_limiting: No direct in-vivo human radical assay located
Inherits M-01b: the electron delivery the claim presupposes is itself NOT ESTABLISHED

evidence_items.text: Oschman 2007 and Oschman, Chevalier & Brown 2015 propose electron-donation antioxidant action as a mechanism.
evidence_items.why_it_matters: Theoretical basis only; narrative reviews by the core author network, not independent synthesis.

evidence_items.text: Giulivi & Kotz 2025: ex-vivo mouse-liver mitochondria showed ATP approximately +5 to 11 percent and H2O2/ROS approximately -22 to 33 percent under reported conditions.
evidence_items.why_it_matters: The strongest concrete antioxidant signal located; it is ex vivo, non-human and cannot demonstrate in-vivo human radical neutralisation.

evidence_items.text: No direct in-vivo human free-radical assay under sham control was located.
evidence_items.why_it_matters: The endpoint the claim names has never been measured in living humans.

evidence_items.text: Lin et al. 2022 reported that the proposed electrochemical signal was non-supportive.
evidence_items.why_it_matters: The one human study that probed a proposed electrochemical intermediate did not support it.

evidence.evidence_sufficiency_rationale: Evidence sits two tiers below the claim: ex-vivo non-human tissue and narrative theory against an asserted in-vivo human event.
supporting: Giulivi & Kotz 2025 ex-vivo mouse-liver ROS/H2O2 reduction

detected.rationale: An ex-vivo mouse-liver mitochondrial ROS signal and a narrative electron-donation theory are used to assert radical neutralisation in living humans.
Evidence tier is cell/ex-vivo non-human; the conclusion tier is an accomplished human biochemical effect.
No validated in-vivo human radical assay under sham control exists in the located evidence.

audit_trail: confidence classified as VALID (no coercion to 0.0)

uncertainty.alternative_label_rationale: An overclaim reading is defensible because the advertisement presents the process under 'has been shown to'. mechanism_vs_evidence is taken as primary because the definitional trigger is squarely present: a described biochemical pathway evidenced only ex vivo and in narrative theory is used to assert an event in living humans.
uncertainty.ambiguity: NONE MATERIAL — the layers agree on the tier gap and differ only on how much credit the ex-vivo signal deserves.

scope_limitations: Adjudication is bounded to the frozen evidence substrate at the 2026-08-22 cut-off. No new literature discovery was performed.
The ASA regulatory outcome is quarantined and contributes no scientific inference.
unresolved_questions: A validated in-vivo human radical assay under sham control has not been performed.

verdict.classification_note: A forensic classification describes the relationship between the claim and the cited evidence. It is not, by itself, proof that the claim is factually false.

verdict.verdict_summary: Free-radical neutralisation by grounding-delivered electrons is a theoretical proposal supported ex vivo in non-human tissue. No validated in-vivo human radical assay under sham control was located, and the proposition also inherits the unestablished provenance step (M-01b).
verdict.verdict_title: Biological or preclinical evidence is presented as human clinical benefit
